messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-18422 — 'redis_maxclients_reached' on redis-prod-1 (us-west-1). metric: maxclients=10000 current=10012. Related alert: 'pg_conn_pool_exhausted' on pg-primary.

pagerduty: Incident PD-18422 created (P1) — Database/cache saturation; escalation policy: oncall-sre. Notifying SRE rotation pager.

irina: Acked. I'm oncall for SRE. Triage starting.

sam: Looking at dashboards. Spike in redis client count at 09:12 UTC, sustained. Postgres active connections jumped from ~260 to ~640.

jake: Deployed recs v3 last night, heavy fanout + per-user connections, might be culprit.

maria: @irina @sam send me the outputs for redis INFO and pg_stat_activity. I'll inspect locks and long-running txns.

sam: Quick dump:
```
# redis
redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 INFO clients
connected_clients:10012
blocked_clients:18
used_memory_human:12.4G
maxclients:10000

# postgres
psql -c 'select count(*) from pg_stat_activity;'
 count 
-------
   640
(1 row)
```

sam: Also seeing many app pods holding idle-open DB connections. No pgbouncer in front of this service.

irina: Any customer impact metrics?

alex (support): We're getting elevated 502/504s for several tenants on bulk write endpoints; about 5% error rate since 09:15 UTC. Priority customers affected: tenant-a, tenant-c.

maria: I'm seeing many idle transactions from user 'recs_service'. I can kill the top offenders. We should be cautious.

jake: recs-service creates one DB connection per worker; config omitted connection pool. Bad.

sam: Short-term mitigation plan:
- Rate-limit /bulk-sync and write-heavy endpoints at the ingress to 60r/min and return 429 for excess.
- Kill runaway idle DB sessions owned by recs_service (low impact ones), staggered.
- Adjust Redis eviction policy to volatile-lru temporarily and flush large ephemeral keys for recs_service.
- Enable circuit-break in recs-service to serve stale cached responses for non-critical flows.

irina: I'll apply ingress rule now. Maria, coordinate on safe DB kills; Sam, prep kill list and playbook. Jake, prepare hotfix to add pgbouncer or pool config.

maria: Running query to list top users:
```
select usename, count(*) from pg_stat_activity group by usename order by count desc limit 10;
recs_service | 338
web_service  | 120
analytics    |  45
```

sam: Killing 20 oldest idle recs_service sessions now, starting with query ids: 15432,15433,15434... will wait 30s between kills and monitor error rate.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-18422 acknowledged by irina at 09:21 UTC.

alex (support): After initial kills and ingress rate-limit, error rate dropped to ~1.6% and redis connected_clients down to ~9,800. Still above maxclients threshold but trending down.

jake: quick note: recs-service will need configuration change to use pool size <= 20 per process, otherwise it will spin up too many conns. I'll open a PR.

irina: Triage update: short-term measures in place; monitoring. Escalation to oncall-db if errors do not fall <1% in 15m. Preparing post-incident follow-ups: customer outreach draft, rollout rollback plan for recs v3, and infra changes (pgbouncer, ingress rate limits, redis eviction tuning).

sam: Adding follow-up tasks to incident ticket: add pgbouncer for recs-service, enforce connection pool in app, add reconnection/backoff in redis client, add SLO alert to page before reaching 80% of maxclients.

maria: I'll hold off on more DB kills unless latency or deadlocks appear. Recording the session ids we killed to ticket.

irina: Thanks all. Keep posting updates in this thread. I'll hand off to night oncall in 2h.

pagerduty: PD-18422 status: acknowledged.
